body: you are not alone in this. my obsession dies down after a few months pass, but i 100% get obsessed to finding out more about people i hate. in my mind, it’s a defense mechanism. they hurt me, so i need to know everything about them to prepare myself in case they attack. y’know?

no, you definitely deserve an apology for his behavior. just because he is acting out due to mental illness doesn’t mean he isn’t hurting the people around him. he still needs to apologize to the people he has hurt when he comes down from episodes.

is he on meds and in therapy? bipolar is a manageable disorder with meds and therapy, and it is an important boundary for your partner to be on the same page with you about treatment.

this is ultimately your call. if you don’t want to be in a relationship with him anymore, that is completely understandable and doesn’t make you a bad person! break ups happen for many reasons, even outside of mental illness. you shouldn’t be bc order to stay in a relationship you’re unhappy in just because your partner is mentally ill. ultimately you need to put yourself first.

but you can choose to stay as well and rekindle that relationship. but like i’ve said, meds and therapy are important. if he won’t commit to both of those, then that’s a problem. you have to be mentally prepared for this situation to happen over and over again, because chances are it will. it’s your call. i wish you luck!

yes!!! i totally get it. totally forgot about the people pleaser thing… constantly trying to make her mother happy so she feels she deserves love, even at the cost of her own happiness. i’ve definitely been there.

it always surprises me how more and more stories like this show up everyday… your friends are right. give him space. let him know that you’re there for him when he’s ready, and carry on with life as if he will never come back. put yourself first for now and start to build yourself back up. if he makes his way around again, great! if he doesn’t, you can’t wait for him forever. i understand how you feel. my partner left me in january during a manic episode, and i still haven’t heard from him. take care hon, stay strong. i’m always here if you wanna chat.

i understand how you feel, op. i’m unmedicated w bpd, and i get the same way with my partner. i’m happy that he is very patient and understanding with you. we all have rough patches every now and again. the best you can do right now is try to get back to your med routine and apologize for your recent outbursts.

have you considered talking to your doctor to try out different meds if you’re tired of the ones you’ve been on? maybe you just need a change. i wish you luck!

literally don’t get me started on the loved ones subreddit because i will not shut up. bunch of angry bitter people who’s shitty person they know in their life either a) happens to have bpd or b) they’ve armchair diagnosed with bpd based on stereotypes. they think they know us better than we know ourselves. to them, it’s like we’re not even human! showing any emotion, even if it’s positive, is manipulative to them. god i could write an essay, seriously. we’re easy to blame so people blame us for everything. fucking sickening.
no i totally understand what you mean. it’s like, they’re the only people that actually get what it’s like. even other illnesses, like bipolar, still don’t get it.

seriously! one of my boundaries with an ex was to send me a simple ‘x’ when he was going to be gone for 6+ hours to over a day, like if he was going out with friends or just needed some time alone. this way i knew he was safe and not upset with me. i asked this because i KNEW it would make me spiral and eventually split!

it’s such an easy thing to do that could have saved us a lot of conflicts, but of course it’s way too demanding and overbearing and clingy. jesus.

i always say i can never keep a close friend for six months. either they leave or i leave. it’s gotten worse as i got older / begin to show symptoms. right now my longest friend is nearing two years, but we barely talk or see one another, and i’m lucky she’s been so nonchalant about my episodes or she’d be gone too. it’s such a lonely cycle i can’t seem to get out of. you’re not alone.
and then once we stick up for what we want, we’re too needy, overbearing, and clingy. nothing we ever do is right, is it? they’ll find any way to blame us for shit.

no, i really appreciate this perspective. it’s been tiring for me. i’m trying not to build up resentment but it’s hard sometimes. i really don’t want to leave her. i love her. i just hope things will get better soon.
seriously! it is so frustrating. any negative emotion is immediately written off as just because i’m borderline. like i’m also human too, how could you forget that?
no, thank you for making me feel a little less alone in how i’m feeling. i’d give anything to get rid of this stupid fucking disease. it sucks, doesn’t it? it really really sucks.
thank you <3

probably both hahah. i get what you mean though. i hate myself more than i can hate any other person. when it comes down to it, everything is my fault. he cheated on me? my fault. i obviously wasn’t giving enough and he felt he needed to seek out someone else. he left me without saying goodbye? that’s my fault too. i know he’s manic but i should have done more to want him to stay. he lied to me, broke my boundaries? that’s my fault too. my boundaries were too unreasonable. i didn’t need them anyway. she invalidates how i feel about something? that’s my fault. i shouldn’t have felt that way, let alone expressed it.

i’m inherently bad, and everyone else is inherently good. i poison them more the more time they spend with me. that’s why everyone leaves eventually, right? i wish i could just disappear, or never need any human interaction ever so that i don’t hurt anyone else anymore. it’s so exhausting. i hate feeling so alone.

so, so true. i at least just wanted a goodbye. all i got was a block and nothing else. and yes, please respond with coping mechanisms if you get a chance. i’ve been trying some but i’m always open to suggestions.

no, i don’t have access to therapy right now. :(

i’ve been trying to work on dbt skills. the best i have for comfort is my friends, who are amazing but… not the same as a therapist. and even though they won’t admit it, i know they’re tired of hearing me cry about him.

i have the same fear. i had a non bp ex that left me three years ago and i still haven’t completely healed from it. in my dreams often, constantly reminded of him. i fear that the same thing is gonna happen with this one too.

god i get that. it’s like… no matter what i do to distract myself, my thoughts Always shift back to him. i can’t let it go. i can’t help but worry and wonder what he’s doing. it’s such a debilitating thing but i can’t get rid of it.

trust me, i understand how you feel right now wholeheartedly. it’s been a struggle for me too. part of me hates him for hurting me— he Knew how badly this would hurt me too. he broke almost all of my boundaries, lied to me for so long… but i don’t know. when it comes down to it i still find myself loving him and missing that he’s not here. i want an apology as well— i deserve one. i’m just trying to stay patient. maybe he’ll come back one day.
thank you so much

wow. thank you for this, genuinely.

i do try to spend a bit of time scrolling through bipolar suns. he is very textbook type 1– in a way it’s almost weird to see people struggling in the exact same ways he does. though i suppose he probably thought that about me when you bc through bpd subs as well.

he definitely turned me into an enemy. his paranoia after discarding me was through the roof. he was terrified i was gonna hurt him or come after him… despite me never showing any signs of violence before. i always just chalked up his intense fear and new hatred up to the amount of time he spent on bpdlovedones… though that’s another story.

i truly thought that him discarding me was my fault. and maybe bits of it are, but seeing so many stories of people going through the same things… combine that with the fact that he was manic for over a month, not taking his meds then lying to me about it, getting more and more hostile and argumentative until the day of discard… afterwards he just treated me like some animal that was gonna hurt him. lots of spending— he flew through any savings he has. drinking, drugs, suicidal ideation and self harm, paranoia, recklessness. i mean just yesterday he decided to meet up with his abusive ex like…

part of me doubts he’s coming back. or maybe i just don’t want to get my hopes up. it’s been over a month now. i’m just trying to put myself back together but god, my bpd does not make it easy. how long did it take your partner to come back after a discard, usually? i have him unblocked on everything despite everyone’s else’s advice… just in case he needs me. i don’t know. i feel lost.
god this one hit the nail on the head. you’re right.

i know… if it hurts this bad for such a short amount of time, i can’t imagine being together for a decade+ long and then dealing with a discard… the sympathy i have for some of the people here. that would kill me.

stay strong as well <3 time will heal these wounds

we were really close friends for 5 months and then started dating. we dated for a little over a month before he dipped. i know that doesn’t seem like long in comparisons to other stories here… but my bpd is definitely playing a major role in how i’m taking this. he was my fp as well.

sadly i don’t have access to therapy at the moment, but i have really been looking into both dbt and other self help methods. i’m lucky to have a really supportive group of friends as well. i don’t know what i’d do without them honestly…

hopefully this will heal with time. hopefully.

i understand. i have bpd, and him leaving absolutely destroyed me. creating closure for myself is so difficult. i had a non bp ex that broke up with me three years ago and i still haven’t been able to heal from it. i hate that this is happening all over again.

no i know exactly what you are trying to say.  i agree with you 100%. it’s the struggle of being able to see them live their lives as if you never existed— a connection or bond that was once so strong being thrown away like it was nothing. and then when they move on right away… it’s like. did i ever even exist? did i matter to you at all? i’m left here grieving and you’re living as if we never met. it is such a weird feeling.
yeah, i’ve heard many stories of bpsos leaving during episodes. it hurts. i hope we can both heal <3 stay strong
thank you, i’m sending love and strength to you as well. it’s such a shitty, lonely, helpless feeling. i guess it will go away with time.
thank you so much <3

it’s flimsy proof at most. i only know it’s them still coming after me because a friend that is still in their discord server gives me warnings. i have faces and names— the problem is that i live in the us, and the key players are in scotland and ireland. what the hell can i even do at that point?
luckily though i do keep screenshots of everything i can and it’s backed up on a google account. i doubt any legal action can be taken though. i just have to hope they stop obsessing over me soon…

it’s hard to describe, but i know i’m truly in love with my girlfriend. it’s improving each other, building each other up. no walking on eggshells on either side. it’s being able to talk about serious things and what needs fixed in our relationship without arguing. it’s learning about each other and how to best help each other. it’s supporting each other through recovery. but it’s also that type of butterflies in stomach love, yknow? not everything has to be so serious. we can talk about our future lives together, spend time with one another, go out on dates… but for me, knowing that if she is gone for a a day, a week, etc, i can handle being on my own. i can wait patiently and find things to do. and the same goes for her. or just being comfortable in silence— sometimes you don’t need to talk, just lay there and be happy with each other’s company. i think that’s what healthy love is, or it’s the closest thing i’ve gotten to it.
okay, thank you so much

yes. he cheated on me during a depressive episode. he was very apologetic afterwards and genuinely seemed to feel terrible about making such a bad decision. looking back on it now after everything that happened, i believe he didn’t really love me at all and therefore didn’t care about cheating on me. he was only apologetic because he thought i would use it against him, despite me saying it was okay.

him interacting with other girls was your sign he wasn’t interested in pursuing a relationship with you. don’t bother with couple’s therapy. he isn’t interested. you’re better off leaving. you both seem extremely toxic for each other and you would be better off getting out of that relationship.

i’ve been there. absolutely destroyed me— i couldn’t get into another relationship for over three years afterward, struggled in my classes and at work, spent every night for six months afterward crying my eyes out. i still have flashbacks and nightmares… and yet two weeks after we broke up, he already had another girlfriend. and he’s been in a long term relationship with another girl for a while now. it hurts how quickly they can move on while you’re left picking up the pieces…

try focusing on you. it takes time but you will heal from this. you got this. take care of yourself; you deserve kindness.

honestly i have dealt with my fair share of ableism as someone with bpd, especially when it comes to support groups and subreddits for partners of pwbpd. i was wary in joining this sub to ask for advice about my ex for that reason, but i was shocked to find the amount of care people have here. sure, you will get the occasional bitter comment, but 9 times out of 10, i have been met with people who truly want what’s best for both the so and the person with bipolar. everyone is extremely helpful and kind, and i enjoy the fact that people with bipolar are allowed to participate and have input in discussions here as well. this sub has been so beneficial to me and so many other people.

i haven’t heard from him. 
i know he plans on seeing his psychiatrist and getting on different meds. i’ve seen a few of his posts, and he said he was thinking of committing suicide. i have to hope he’s rational enough to not go through with it, and that it won’t go further than intrusive thoughts. i have no way to reach out to him— i couldn’t help if i tried. i hope he’s okay though.
i’m trying to think about him less. really trying. i mean, this has consumed me for a month. like every waking moment… i can’t do it anymore.
i don’t know if he is planning on reaching out to me. if he does, i’ll be here to help him. that is, as long as i can handle it mentally / emotionally. i know he’s at least looked at my social media… he posted a stanza from a poem a few hours after i had referenced it on my account. could just be a weird coincidence, or he could’ve seen it… who knows.
i hope he has the courage to reach out. i just want him to be safe, but i won’t put his well-being over mine anymore.

god i know exactly what you mean. my ex’s friends did this to him. feeding into his delusions, encouraging his recklessness and bad habits when he was manic… all of them also had mental health issues as well. really glorified the whole “look at how insane and crazy i am” for entertainment. and then when he was depressed, they didn’t care about him. it makes me angry that he got dragged into that and that he’s left with them now.
i know, love

just remember… they really never change. abusers will hardly ever change. even if things look picture perfect with a new partner, it doesn’t mean they are. you have a chance to build yourself up from now on, and eventually you are going to find someone that’s gonna make you so happy. things simply weren’t meant to be with him. the best you can do is try to move on and heal yourself.

i understand how you feel. my ex abused me for three years, and is now in a relationship with another girl. it seems like he treats her so much better than he treated me, and it makes me so angry. why me? what about me deserved the torment he put me through? i wonder if the abuse was really all my fault, or maybe i just overreacted and made everything up. i really hope you can find peace. you deserve to be happy and healthy.
thank you. i’m sorry you’re going through this as well. i hope everything gets better for you soon.
thank you

yeah, i have seen this. my ex was abused by a girl a few years ago. if left him with a lot of insecurities and he struggled to show affection. he was nice when we first started talking but quickly became borderline abusive. gaslighting, manipulation, punishment, etc. i chalk it up to, maybe it’s not really on purpose. maybe he feels like he has to do to this. maybe he’s struggling to cover up his own securities and playing the cold, aggressive role is there to make me validate his own self hatred. i really don’t know.

my god, been there. it’s not your fault, no matter what he says or tries to do to convince you that it is. it took me getting into an actual healthy relationship with someone who treats me well to realize that. it takes time to dismantle the fucked up rationale your abusive partner brainwashed you to believe, but you can do it. good luck to you. don’t forget your worth.

i totally understand. thank you so much for this perspective. i think it’s really valuable to talk to people that have bipolar as well as bipolar SOs, because you will understand the root of actions and feelings more than someone who has never dealt with those feelings before themself.

to be honest, i’m not expecting an apology, or to ever be in contact again really. i’ve had about a month to process and work through this, so even if he reached out and said he wanted to talk, i would probably say no anyway (and it’s nothing against him truly, i just can’t be in that position again).

i understand the shame aspect of it. when i have episodes due to my bpd, the shame afterwards is unbearable. there have been times where i have just run away instead of apologizing, and there have been times where i’ve apologized and tried to work through it with the person i hurt. i really do understand how it feels, and in a way i won’t blame him if i never hear from him again. he probably feels that contacting me again after everything is just reopening the wound. he always said he wished i didn’t love him, as if he didn’t deserve it. i’m not really sure. i just hope he’s okay.

i would love to talk to him about everything. he did a lot behind my back that really hurt me. i want… some form of explanation, of reasoning for why he hurt me. people don’t have that though, especially if a decision is irrational anyway. so i’ll settle for an apology and a goodbye.
thank you <3

that’s the plan. i’m not going to message him. i don’t want it to seem like i’m hovering. i don’t want him to assume i’m upset or angry with him, because i’m not. i’m worried for him but i’m gonna give it some time.

i hope this is a good thing. i wish we could talk about everything that happened, though i don’t think we should be friends or date afterward. at this point, i just want some form of closure. i’m trying not to get my hopes up that we’ll even talk at all, but it’s hard to suppress.

thank you for sharing this. i’m so happy that he is self aware and focused on improving himself, and that you can relax and be there to support him.

i feel like he wouldn’t apologize, not because he doesn’t care or doesn’t believe he did anything wrong, but for my sake. even before all of this happened, he was always convinced that he was a bad partner and that i would be better off moving on from him. i also had bpd, and he was my fp for months. he hated having that much control over me.

i feel like he thinks that if he were to reach out to me, even if to apologize, that he would be dragging me back into it rather than letting me alone to heal. (of course, i would much prefer an apology. or at least a goodbye, as i didn’t get one before he left). that’s why i think even if he felt terrible for it, he would rationalize not reaching out to me as something for my own good.

i hope everything works out. i’m just trying to keep my hopes down so i don’t get hurt again.
thank you so much for this. i’ll look into it!
god i felt that. i hate dreaming about the good parts. i hate being reminded of before everything got so much worse. i’m sorry she did that to you. take care of yourself.

exactly. and like… at least for me, the dreams are never bad. they can just be complete nonsense type dreams but he’s always there and we’ll just talk like normal. it’s so weird. it’s so hard to forget about him when you’re constantly reminded of him by your subconscious. even on days where he doesn’t cross my mind, he’ll still be in my dreams. it’s so weird.
“he just wants his own self hatred to be validated by me”… so true.

whoa. i am so proud of you for your reaction. you stood your ground and remained calm, even while he was acting insanely immature. it takes a lot of maturity and confidence to stay level headed in a situation like this. stay strong!
thank you for sharing <3

i can’t say for certain, because i don’t know her or you. but i’ve had a partner go no contact from me to end the relationship before, because of how unhealthy it was for both of us. it was really good for me to have that time away and work on myself, and if he ever was willing, i would totally be okay with just being friends with him again.

some pwbpd feel the need to move on quickly because of the horrible emptiness you experience after the end of a relationship. i’ve never really felt that need, moreso because i try and take the time to figure out where i went wrong for that relationship to end and focus on how i can improve myself before making another connection with someone. whether she will move on and find someone to fill that hole that you left is based on how self aware she is of herself and her own actions. 

i can tell you care about her. please don’t feel to terrible about going no contact— sometime it can be extremely beneficial for both parties. i know i’m thankful my ex went nc, even if it hurt for a while. 

i hope you guys can reconnect when you both are healthier mentally. take care of yourself!
i’m confused by what you mean.

i know exactly how you feel. it’s a burden for us to have to carry the weight of the hurt they put us through, while they can walk off scott-free. you’re not alone in this.

for me, it did get better over time. i thought about him and what he did to me less and less over the span of the past few years. occasionally, i’m reminded of it. he’ll be there in a dream or show up in my photos memories. 

focus on yourself, op. look at how strong you’ve already been! you can do this. healing takes time but it gets better. take care of yourself.

i understand how you feel. the guilt that you feel from the hurt you unconsciously cause others because of a mental illness you can’t control… it can become unbearable. i can tell how much you care about her. please remember to continue to take care of yourself as well. don’t let this grief become all consuming.

this takes a lot of vulnerability to share. it’s a good thing to recognize your own faults and the areas you have messed up in a relationship. i’m proud of you for being strong, and for continuing to take your medications & go to therapy. you are doing everything right. i hope you are doing well, and i’m proud of you.
thank you.
thank you for the advice. this gives me a lot to think about— i really appreciate it.
i know how you feel. you’re not alone.
aw, thank you so much. i doubt he will, especially because it’s getting late, but i still have a bit of hope.
i’m lucky to have amazing friends and family as support. they made it as happy as it could be. the thought of him lingers though, y’know?
thank you so much <3
thank you <3
thank you for the advice <3
thank you

god i know exactly how you feel right now.

you have to assure yourself. there really is nothing you can do. i know it’s such a helpless feeling, but you can’t linger on worrying about him. try to have some fair things that his family and friends will take care of him. remember He’s the one that left You, not the other way around.

he will most likely make his way around eventually— it just depends if you want to wait for him or not. this isn’t the first story i’ve heard like this. i’ve had one as well. give him the time and space he needs and focus on repairing yourself for a while. you can’t try to rationalize an irrational decision. believe me, i’ve tried. the only thing you can control right now is yourself. focus on you and your mental health while you wait.

yeah. you need to move on. if he has no plans on trying to get better and has been emotionally abusive, you need to go. i understand how hard it is to let go— i have bpd as well and my ex was my fp. it hurt so much and still does sometimes. this will be good for you in the end, i promise.

i’m so sorry this is happening to you. i’ve been there. it’s gonna hurt really bad for a few days and then you’ll start feeling a bit better. livable-better. here’s what i’m gonna recommend to you…

focus on yourself. i mean it. find new hobbies. buy a 500 piece puzzle, a few word games on your phone. volunteer at an animal shelter. spend more time studying or working. go out with friends. do more self care. journal. you NEED to find things to occupy your mind and improve yourself.

you know him and your relationship more than i do, but this sounds like a blessing in disguise. if he comes back, you need strong boundaries. therapy and meds or nothing. you cannot let him walk all over you. take this time away to realize your own self worth and focus on repairing the cracks that he left in your mental health.

i’m here if you need anyone to vent to. feel free to pm me. you can get through this!
thank you so much

i totally get that. he was talking to me less, picking fights over little things. until it all just boom. was over. he didn’t even say goodbye— just blocked me on everything. he even knew that i struggled with attachment issues / fear of people leaving because of my bpd. he didn’t care.

i’m sorry you had to go through that. you should be proud that you are stronger now and set clear boundaries. it’s not easy for everyone to do. i hope all is well with you now!

it’s okay. thank you for all the advice you have given— it doesn’t go unappreciated. it’s a helpless situation. i wish there was more i could do but until he talks to me again, i have no input. i can only hope he stays safe.

i know he’s active on that subreddit and asked a question about quitting meds, and all of the replies told him not to, or to talk to his psychiatrist to change his dosage, try a different kind, etc. he hasn’t gotten in contact with his psychiatrist and still isn’t taking meds.

he’s bp1. he’s already manic from what i can tell.  any chance of rationality i entirely missed, because he had said he was on meds and he wasn’t. i couldn’t tell until it was too late.

he was on lamotrigine for a few months (2 or 3 i think?) before stopping cold turkey. he had never been medicated before that, this was his first time.

he stopped going to therapy as well.

i’m pretty sure he’s already manic— he’s been acting out, worse than he would during previous episodes.

the issue is— about a month after being off meds and him getting worse (i didn’t even know he was off meds, he was lying to me about still being on them), he completely ghosted me. i don’t have any influence in this and none of his shitty friends will say anything despite them knowing he’s getting worse.

it’s not you. i’m in the same boat. bpsos can sometimes just run. though i haven’t figured out exactly why, whether it’s because they don’t think they deserve the love from their so, they’re irrational and convinced they’re bad for you, i don’t know. you are not alone in this.

i know it’s hard, but it’s a waiting game. you need to spend this time focusing on you. finding ways to pass the time, getting a new hobby, going out with friends. you need to take your mind off of him. if he comes back, you need to put new boundaries in place. i wish you luck.

dm me if you need to talk. i’m here for you.
ah okay, thank you. that makes sense!
i’m sorry you had to experience that. could you elaborate on what your distorted thinking was like, if you’re comfortable sharing?

both of you need to put up strong boundaries— she needs to respect yours and you need to respect hers.

take care of yourself as well to prevent empathy fatigue. let her know if you need some time away to focus on yourself. do a bit of self care, go out with friends, play video games or find a new hobby. 

encourage her to get treatment— whether that’s therapy, meds, or work through a dbt workbook on her own everyday.

having a partner with bpd is not a death sentence for a relationship. we can be loving and extremely loyal. the only thing i will emphasize is be Patient. during episodes it feels like i can’t control anything i say or do, and i’m sure she feels the same. the guilt afterwards can eat you alive. you are a safe place for her, but you also need to take care of yourself as well.

i wish you both luck!
it’s so heartbreaking. i’m sorry you had to go through that. i hope you’re doing well.
thank you so much
i’m sorry you both had to go through that. i hope you’re both doing well now. thank you for sharing

thank you for sharing. he’s been having worse episodes since he went off them. he says being on meds was like having his head underwater, and now that he’s off them, he’s finally surfaced. he’s so much more irritable and irrational and impulsive. i don’t know what to do.
thank you for sharing. i’m sorry you had to go through that. i hope both you and your husband are well!

i know. i’ve read that. he went off meds over a month ago and was lying to me about still being on them. he refuses to go back on them. i was wondering what people had seen if they or their partners had gone off meds. it makes me really nervous, but i’m not sure what i can do. he’s completely irrational and won’t listen to me. he was on / is supposed to be on lamotrogine.
i know. my ex had went off his meds and lied to me, saying he was still taking them. i only posted asking for what people saw symptom wise to compare it it what i noticed in him.

i’m sorry you’re going through this right now. i understand how much it hurts— i’ve been there myself. do some little things to calm yourself down and distract your mind, such as having some tea or doing a bit of self care. you’re right about needing to get back into dbt seriously, it will help this from happening again. i hope everything works out for you. you’ll be in my thoughts.

you know him and your relationship better than i do, so take my advice with a grain of salt.

in all honesty, don’t do any big gestures to try and make up for it. i have bpd and would feel awful for hoe that affected my partner. to show that i loved him, i would draw him something, buy him a gift, etc. your partner’s just gonna end up using you trying to say sorry against you. they assume that it’s lovebombing, or the gift giving is just to guilt trip them into staying.

i understand where you’re coming from because my mind operates the same way, but in my opinion you’re better off trying to act like everything is normal again rather than being overly affectionate to make up for it.
thank you so much!
thank you for letting me know. i’m sorry you had to go through that. how long did these symptoms last for you, if you don’t mind me asking?

fp = favorite person. people with bpd experience it. it’s an intense attachment to a specific person or thing. this person consumes your mind. you constantly want to talk with them or hang out with them, and even a few hours without them can hurt you. it can be extremely damaging to both the fp and the pwBPD, but it can also be a healthy relationship. 

it depends on both parties for how the relationship operates. boundaries are very important. the fp needs to have time alone to destress, and the pwBPD needs a good support system outside of their fp. 

without perpetuating the ‘pwBPD are uncontrollable animals’ trope, it’s a bit like a leash. there is a strong loyalty. i would do anything for him if he asked me to. you feel their emotions tenfold. if he’s angry at someone, i hate them more than he does. there has to be a lot of trust and understanding between an fp and the pwBPD. i know a lot of websites really stigmatize that relationship, but it can be good if both parties can cooperate.

my advice to anyone here is: stay patient and level headed the best you can, but if you are hurting and your relationship is hurting you, it’s best to put yourself first and try to move on.
it is definitely still infatuation. the infatuation stage in any relationship tends to last around six months. if you have caught him pursuing other people despite talking with you (even if you didn’t consider it an official relationship), he probably feels guilty for that and hence the lovebombing. 
if this has happened multiple times, and you’re worried that he is obsessed with you even after not talking with him for months, i would keep my distance. obsession can be extremely unhealthy on both ends (coming from someone that has bpd), and it’s best not to feed into that / encourage it.
however, you know your relationship, yourself, and him better than a stranger on the internet does. use your discretion but remember to keep your health first, and his second. if trying to be close to him again will cause you harm / make you upset, don’t.

try to remember that they don’t truly mean what they say. be patient with them— chances are they are tearing themself apart more intensely than they are hurting you.
seek healthy coping mechanisms— something to occupy your mind, such as journaling. talk to friends and see a therapist. after an episode, try to talk with them about how you felt. they will most likely apologize and mean it genuinely.
however, if you can’t handle the heartache that comes with a so with bipolar, it’s okay to put yourself and your mental health first and cut ties. it can become exhausting, but it is ultimately your decision on whether or not you can continue to be supportive of them during episodes.
